title: Inverse identifiability closure: actin-force recovery for the ENTH+AP180 construct
construct: ENTH domain + AP180 IDP (predicted productive at ~55 pN actin, from enth_fusion_cases)

setup.prior_note: active-force prior widened to [0,120] pN (default ceiling 60 was tuned for a lower-force regime); 55 pN sits well inside, so the recovery is not a rail artifact.

with_actin_channel.interpretation: The independent actin-density channel (actin intensity proportional to force/ACTIN_CALIB) breaks the c_eff/force degeneracy that H(t) alone cannot resolve, so active force is IDENTIFIED at the true value with a calibrated CI68.

without_actin_channel.interpretation: Without the degeneracy-breaking channel, force trades off against c_eff along an unconstrained direction; the identifiability firewall correctly REFUSES a point value (identified=False) rather than reporting the biased median.

sigma_note: Membrane tension (sigma) is unidentifiable from single-CCP geometry in both cases (width ratio ~0.99), consistent with the recovery-calibration gate.
verdict: Closes the identifiability loop for ENTH+AP180: curvo recovers the known 55 pN actin force at 55.0 pN median (bias -0.1%) with a calibrated CI68 (coverage 0.75) ONLY when the actin degeneracy-breaking channel is present; without it, force is refused. This is the operational meaning of the anti-force-astrology firewall -- a physics-grounded, uncertainty-calibrated force where an observable constrains it, and an honest refusal where it does not.
caveat: Synthetic-data recovery test: the trajectory is generated by the same forward model used in the inverse, so this validates the ENGINE and identifiability logic (self-consistency, calibration, degeneracy handling), not the real-imaging perception front-end. A real ENTH+AP180 fusion experiment would additionally require the epi-TIRF / STAR depth observable and a co-imaged actin channel.
